**Aarhus Universitetshospital** is a major hospital located in [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], Denmark. It is extensively evaluated in the 2022–2023 annual report from the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK), published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP), which monitors the quality of cardiovascular care across the Danish healthcare system [^src1] [^src2]. 

During the reporting period of July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023, the hospital's performance was measured against several national clinical quality standards for newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients. Notably, for [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], which tracks the proportion of patients receiving an echocardiogram, Aarhus Universitetshospital achieved a rate of 83.5% (95% CI: 80.7–86.1), successfully meeting the national standard of ≥80% [^src2]. For [[indikator-4a|Indikator 4a]], which measures anticoagulation treatment coverage, the hospital reported a treatment rate of 87.3% (95% CI: 83.0–90.8) [^src3]. 

The hospital's data is also crucial for tracking adverse outcomes and complications. Within one year of diagnosis, the proportion of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients at the hospital who experienced severe bleeding ([[indikator-12|Indikator 12]]) was 4.6% (95% CI: 3.3–6.1) [^src7]. Furthermore, the one-year mortality rate ([[indikator-13|Indikator 13]]) for these patients was recorded at 16.4% (95% CI: 14.1–18.9) [^src7]. The hospital is consistently listed across various other indicators in the report—including ischemic stroke, intracranial bleeding, and heart failure—highlighting its role as a key institution in Denmark's systematic clinical quality benchmarking and healthcare monitoring [^src1] [^src6] [^src8].
